draft.title: The Spartan army
card: a heavily armed citizen soldier. He carried a large round shield, a spear and a short sword, and wore a bronze helmet and body armour.
a tight block of hoplites standing in rows, shoulder to shoulder. Each man's shield partly covered the man on his left, so the line worked only if everyone held their place.

Spartan men trained for war from boyhood under the state system, and they were full-time soldiers as adults. This made their drill and discipline better than that of most Greek armies, which were part-time citizen soldiers.
Spartans were trained to hold the line and not to retreat. This discipline made the Spartan army the most feared in Greece.
draft.remember: Spartan strength came from discipline: trained hoplites holding the phalanx together.

a.q: Why did a phalanx depend so much on discipline?
opts: Each hoplite's shield helped cover the man beside him
Each hoplite fought alone and chose his own enemy
Each hoplite relied on archers to break the enemy line
Each hoplite was protected by cavalry on both flanks
a.why: Shields overlapped, so the line was strong only while every man held his place. A hoplite did not fight as a free individual, which is why the second option is wrong.
a.clue: Think about whose side each shield protected.

b.q: Two Greek armies of hoplites meet in a phalanx. One is full-time, trained from boyhood. The other is made of part-time farmers. Which is more likely to keep its line under pressure?
opts: The trained army, because years of drill built discipline
The farmer army, because its men own larger shields
The trained army, because it avoids fighting in a phalanx
The farmer army, because its men are fighting for pay
b.why: Long training made soldiers used to holding formation, as the Spartans were. The farmers used the same kind of shield and phalanx, so shield size does not decide it, and the trained army did fight in a phalanx.
b.clue: Which army practised holding its place the most?

a.best: Each hoplite's shield helped cover the man beside him

b.best: The trained army, because years of drill built discipline

problems.detail: Too easy for Year 12. The stem itself describes one army as full-time and trained from boyhood, and the three distractors are implausible: 'fighting for pay' contradicts 'part-time farmers', and 'avoids fighting in a phalanx' contradicts the stem. A student can answer without knowing the idea.

proposal.title: The Spartan army
card: a heavily armed citizen soldier. He carried a large round shield, a spear and a short sword, and wore a bronze helmet and body armour. Most Greek city-states fought with hoplites.
a tight block of hoplites standing in rows, shoulder to shoulder. Each man's shield partly covered the man on his left, so the line worked only if everyone held their place.

Spartan men trained for war from boyhood under the state system, and they were full-time soldiers as adults. This made their drill and discipline better than that of most Greek armies, which were part-time citizen soldiers.
Spartans were trained to hold the line and not to retreat. This discipline made the Spartan army the most feared in Greece.
proposal.remember: Spartan strength came from discipline: trained hoplites holding the phalanx together.

a.q: Why did a phalanx depend so much on discipline?
opts: Each hoplite's shield helped cover the man beside him
Each hoplite fought alone and chose his own enemy
Each hoplite relied on archers to break the enemy line
Each hoplite was protected by cavalry on both flanks
a.why: Shields overlapped, so the line was strong only while every man held his place. A hoplite did not fight as a free individual, which is why the second option is wrong.
a.clue: Think about whose side each shield protected.

b.q: Spartan and Athenian hoplites carried the same kind of shield and spear. What best explains why the Spartan army was more feared?
opts: Spartans trained full-time from boyhood, so held the line
Spartans were citizen soldiers, while others were hired men
Spartans used a looser line that let each man fight freely
Spartans were drilled to fall back early and then regroup
b.why: With the same equipment, the difference was training: full-time drill from boyhood gave Spartans the discipline to hold the phalanx. The citizen soldier option is tempting, but most Greek armies were also made of citizen soldiers, so that did not set Sparta apart.
b.clue: If the gear was the same, what was different about the men?

a.best: Each hoplite's shield helped cover the man beside him

b.best: Spartans trained full-time from boyhood, so held the line
